page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth remains stable at average tiers, reaching 75.3 GB/sec for large-block read operations, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme single-threaded CPU speeds. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks. The instance achieves average performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving, making it a viable option for memory-bound enterprise applications, web serving, and basic text or image processing pipelines.
